blocks.intro: Old buildings and shared walls shape most calls.

items.body: Pipes on exterior walls and back porches freeze first.
Like July 2011, when basements flooded across the neighborhood.
A failed line upstairs reaches the unit below.

blocks.h2: What You Get When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: Fast help and a price first.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: In a shared building, one unit's emergency quickly becomes everyone's. Know where your unit's shutoff is, and where the building main is. In many two-flats, it's in the basement near the meter. Keep a phone number for the other owners or the association. If water is coming through a ceiling, it's probably from the unit above. Shut off what you can, warn your neighbors and call us.

blocks.h2: Emergencies During a Chicago Cold Snap
blocks.body: When temperatures drop below zero, our calls shift to frozen and burst pipes, especially on enclosed back porches and kitchen walls in older buildings. Keep the heat steady, open cabinet doors and let a faucet drip. If a pipe bursts, shut off the water at your unit's valve or the building main and call us.

blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.answer: Yes. Our phone line is open around the clock.

items.q: Water is leaking into the unit below. What do I do?
items.preview: Shut off your water and call us.
items.answer: Close the fixture shutoff or your unit's main valve, then call us and let your neighbor know.

items.q: Who do I call if I smell gas?
items.answer: Leave the building and call Peoples Gas or 911 from outside. We'll handle the repair once it's safe.

items.q: Will I know the price first?
items.answer: Yes. You'll approve a flat-rate price before work begins.

items.q: How fast can you get here?
items.answer: We're on Ravenswood Avenue, and we work to get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: Is the leak my responsibility or my neighbor's?
items.answer: It depends on where it starts. We'll find the source. Insurance and the association decide the rest.
